title: Gaze of the Heavenly Eye
next_chapter_hook: In the instant when those eyes that transcended the Heavenly Dao spoke, the remnant soul of Mo Xiansheng on the first page of the Tianji Record shuddered violently, as if recognizing something—and Chen Ji finally heard that voice, calling not 'waste,' not 'servant,' but the name he had never mentioned to anyone.

text.content: In the moment that chess piece fell, Chen Ji felt an extremely faint pulse from deep within the Tianji Record. At first it was like a heartbeat—one beat, two beats—then it transformed into a roaring tsunami, as if something was awakening from ten thousand years of slumber. His fingertips tingled slightly, the pages of the Tianji Record fluttered without wind, and the yellowed edges emanated a sinister golden glow—a color he had never seen since obtaining the fragment.

"It's here." Chen Ji silently recited in his heart. His expression remained calm as still water, as if merely waiting for an expected visitor. But in the depths of his pupils, the Tianji Record hovering before him was reflected—the chess board outlined by Mo Xiansheng's remnant soul suddenly collapsed, replaced by a rift tearing through the void. Within that rift, something was watching him. That gaze was cold, vast, surpassing everything he had ever known.

dialogue.content: (Staring directly at that rift, murmuring in his heart) So you've come, the thing that transcends the Heavenly Dao. I've been waiting for you for a long time.

text.content: Within the void, that rift suddenly expanded. An eye emerged from the depths of the rift—no, that wasn't a single eye. It was a phantom superimposed from countless eyes, each with pupils like abysses, each reflecting different fates. Some saw dynasties rise and fall, some saw stars plummet, some saw沧海桑田—the fate of all things was exposed under that eye's gaze. And Chen Ji finally saw the existence behind that eye.

It was no existence he could comprehend. It had no face, no form, only a constantly writhing sea of consciousness. At the core of that sea of consciousness was this 'Heavenly Eye.' The Heavenly Eye slowly turned, as if examining an ant—no, in its eyes, perhaps not even an ant qualified. But such an existence, across a chess game spanning a hundred thousand years, had treated countless geniuses as chess pieces, the Tianji Record as a tool, and him, Chen Ji... also as a single chess piece.

Chen Ji felt an unprecedented sense of oppression. It wasn't spiritual pressure, wasn't killing intent, but a crushing force from the very nature of existence—as if if it wished, his very existence could be effortlessly erased. Was this the true face of the 'Eye of Heavenly Dao'? Was this the existence that laid out the Tianji Record a hundred thousand years ago? He suddenly understood why all the prognosticators throughout history had gone mad or died—facing such an existence, human will was inherently fragile.

Yet Chen Ji did not close his eyes. He even tugged at the corner of his mouth, revealing a faint, cold smile. "So that's how it is." His voice rang out in the vast Mental Sea, calm as if he weren't facing an existence that transcended the Heavenly Dao, "I've always been wondering what kind of creature the creator of the Tianji Record was. Now I see—it's even more absurd than I imagined. Even the Heavenly Dao is merely your chess piece, so what am I?"

The Heavenly Eye seemed to sense his emotions. The phantom composed of countless vertical pupils slightly contracted, as if reassessing this ant before it. The next moment, an information stream directly poured into Chen Ji's Mental Sea—a scene. In that scene was the vista of ten thousand years ago: countless sects scattered like chess pieces across the vast earth, and above all sects, an invisible giant net笼罩着整片天地. That was the Net of Fate, the source of the laws of the Heavenly Dao, and also... the chessboard laid out by the Eye of Heavenly Dao.

Chen Ji glimpsed merely the tip of that net. The Demonic Path Holy Sect, Xuanwu Sect, Tianqing Sect... the so-called Three Great Sects were nothing but three fruits grown on the web. And the Tianqing Sect where Chen Ji resided was merely the most insignificant of them—because the founder of the Tianqing Sect was the previous generation's 'Tianji Seer' selected by the Eye of Heavenly Dao. That Tianji Seer discovered the truth, attempted to resist, ultimately perished, leaving only a fragmented Tianji Record that fell into Chen Ji's hands.

dialogue.content: (The Heavenly Eye transmits a cold ripple of consciousness) You know too much, Chen Ji. But this is not enough.

text.content: Chen Ji's heart sank sharply. "Chen Ji"—that was his true name. He had never told anyone this name. At the Tianqing Sect, he was 'Waste Servant Chen,' in the eyes of the world, he was 'Trash Chen,' but his true name "Chen Ji" was the deepest secret he concealed. How did it know? Was the Tianji Record itself a tracker? Or had he been watched from the moment he obtained the fragment?

"You bear this name," the Heavenly Eye transmitted again, carrying a hair-raising playfulness, "because on the day of your birth, a Tianji Record fragment flew into the Chen family ancestral home. You thought it was coincidence, not knowing it was my chess piece that I had waited three thousand years for. You carry the bloodline of a Tianji Seer, and your sister is the key to unlocking the final seal—do you think you're the one laying out formations? In truth, you have always been on my chessboard."

choices.description: Since the other party already knows everything, pretending ignorance is pointless. Better to directly question its purpose, hoping to gain more key information from the dialogue.
choices.visible_cost: Expose more information to the other party
choices.visible_reward: May obtain crucial clues about his sister Chen Nian and the complete version of the Tianji Record
choices.risk_hint: The other party may take this opportunity to plant traps or interference in his consciousness

text.content: Chen Ji took a deep breath, staring directly at the Heavenly Eye composed of countless vertical pupils. His voice was calm, yet carried an unnoticeable edge: "Since you know so much, allow me to ask—why tell me all this? Do you want me to become your chess piece, or do you want to see what it looks like when I resist?"

text.content: Chen Ji lowered his eyes, concealing the sharpness within them. He pretended to be intimidated, his voice slightly trembling: "You... what exactly do you want me to do?" But deep in his consciousness, he was rapidly recording every detail of the Heavenly Eye's information transmission—three faint fluctuations when it spoke, which might be its weakness.

choices.description: Immediately mobilize the power of the Tianji Record, attempt to use the ability to foresee the future to see through the other party's intentions. Since it says the Tianji Record is a chess piece it laid out, let the chess piece bite back at its master.
choices.visible_cost: Consumes a large amount of Heavenly Fate points (-15), and the other party may sense the intention
choices.visible_reward: May foresee the other party's next plan, make advance preparations

text.content: Chen Ji appeared obedient on the surface, but was mobilizing the power of the Tianji Record in secret. The fragment grew slightly warm, a familiar force flowing from his fingertips into his Mental Sea—but just as he was about to glimpse the future, the Heavenly Eye suddenly enlarged, those vertical pupils all turning toward him, as if seeing through all his schemes. A terrifying force instantly flooded his consciousness, forcibly interrupting his foresight.

The Heavenly Eye seemed to sense his choice. No matter which approach he chose, that eye transcending the Heavenly Dao showed no emotional fluctuation. It simply watched him silently, as if appreciating a drama whose ending it already knew. "Your choice," it transmitted, "determines your fate from here on. But no matter what you choose, one thing will not change—your sister, Chen Nian, is my final chess piece, and the only variable in your game."

dialogue.content: (The Heavenly Eye transmits a cold ripple of consciousness) Chen Nian, the person you've been searching for. She is not called 'Heavenly Fate Lock Key,' but 'Tianji Box.' Open her, and you will obtain the final page of the Tianji Record—and the true reason for my existence.

text.content: Chen Ji's heart tightened sharply. Chen Nian—his sister who had been missing for years, frail and sickly since childhood, raised by distant relatives, then mysteriously disappeared. He had always thought his sister was simply taken by some force, never expecting her to have such a deep connection to the Tianji Record. What did 'Tianji Box' mean? What would opening her entail? His rationality told him this might be a trap, but as a brother, the longing to find his sister burned like fire in his heart.

The Heavenly Eye seemed to sense the fluctuation in his heart, the phantom composed of countless vertical pupils slightly expanding, as if laughing. "See? Even if you calculate with precision, even if you treat everyone in the world as chess pieces, there are things you still cannot let go. Emotion. This word is the biggest loophole on my chessboard, and your only way out." The Heavenly Eye paused, then transmitted the final piece of information—Chen Nian's current location, and a code only Chen Ji could understand.

text.content: Chen Ji reached out his hand, touching that stream of information. A set of coordinates and a code flooded his consciousness—"The Tianji Box is in the Holy Sect's Forbidden Grounds; the key is a jade pendant engraved with your name." He lowered his head to look at his chest, where hung a jade pendant he had worn since childhood, engraved with two characters: "Chen Ji." He had never imagined this jade pendant had such an origin.

choices.description: The more proactively provided information, the more suspicious. The more the other party wants him to find Chen Nian, the more important finding Chen Nian is to its plan—the less he should let it have its way.
choices.visible_reward: May disrupt the other party's rhythm, gain more time for his own arrangements
choices.risk_hint: The other party may change strategies accordingly, use more aggressive means against Chen Nian

text.content: Chen Ji withdrew his hand, stepping back. His expression remained calm, but his eyes held more coldness: "My sister's affairs don't need you to tell me." The Heavenly Eye slightly contracted, as if reassessing his reaction. After a moment, that rift began to slowly heal. The Heavenly Eye's voice rang out again: "Interesting. You're as proud as the previous Tianji Seer. But you will return, because apart from me, no one can tell you where she is."

At the very last moment before the Heavenly Eye was about to dissipate, that existence transcending the Heavenly Dao suddenly paused. Its vertical pupils ceased rotating, instead all fixating on Chen Ji—that gaze carried an indescribable weight, as if looking at a variable that was about to change the chess game. "Chen Ji," the Heavenly Eye spoke again, this time not with cold ripples of consciousness, but with a true 'voice'—that voice was ancient, primordial, carrying an unnoticeable trace of mockery, "did you think it was coincidence that you encountered me in the eighth volume?"

Chen Ji's pupils contracted sharply. He suddenly realized a problem—he had obtained the Tianji Record for a full eight volumes, and in these eight volumes, he had always thought he was laying formations, calculating, playing the fool to devour tigers. But thinking back now, every 'foresight' where he received information from the Tianji Record had been under its watchful eye. The 'future' he saw—was that really a future he chose himself? Or was it merely a 'future' it wanted him to see? The existence of the Heavenly Eye gave him the first true fear—not fear of power, but fear of 'being manipulated.'

dialogue.content: (The Heavenly Eye transmits one final piece of consciousness, carrying a meaningful smile) However, I quite like you. You're far more interesting than those previous wastes. So, I give you a chance—go find her, open her. By then, you will discover the truth of this world... and the truth of yourself.

text.content: The rift completely healed, and the Heavenly Eye vanished into the void. The Mental Sea returned to its usual tranquility, only the Tianji Record floated before Chen Ji, the chess board on its pages still broken, Mo Xiansheng's remnant soul seemingly fallen into slumber. Chen Ji stood quietly in place, his expression gradually shifting from shock to contemplation, finally settling on a complex smile. "Interesting," he murmured, his voice carrying a trace of self-mockery, "so I was never the chess player after all."

"But what of it?" Chen Ji suddenly laughed, that smile carrying an unexpected lightness. He tucked the Tianji Record back into his sleeve, turning to look out the window. The night at Tianqing Sect remained peaceful, the stars remained brilliant, no one knew what had happened tonight, and no one knew that this 'waste servant' had just encountered an existence transcending the Heavenly Dao. He took a deep breath, murmuring to himself: "You say I'm a chess piece, I accept that. But you forgot one thing—" his gaze gradually sharpened, "a chess piece can also devour the general."

dialogue.content: (Murmuring to himself, eyes flashing with dangerous light) Chen Nian... wait for me. Whether you're the 'Heavenly Fate Lock Key' or the 'Tianji Box,' I will find you. As for you— he looked toward the void, as if conversing across space with that vanished Heavenly Eye—your chess game, I will personally overturn.

text.content: Just then, the Tianji Record suddenly grew slightly warm. Mo Xiansheng's remnant soul awakened from slumber, that blurry face showing a complex expression. "What you just encountered," Mo Xiansheng's voice was low and weary, "is the true face of the 'Eye of Heavenly Dao.' It is not the Heavenly Dao; it is something that transcends the Heavenly Dao—or rather, it is the creator of all Heavenly Dao." He paused, as if hesitating whether to continue, ultimately speaking, "It is called the 'Weaver of Fate's Web,' the earliest indigenous inhabitant of this heavens and earth."

Chen Ji listened quietly, not interrupting. Mo Xiansheng's remnant soul rarely spoke more: "The Tianji Record is its tool for weaving the web of fate, and every generation of Tianji Seers has been its chess piece. But it has a fatal weakness—it cannot directly intervene in the mortal world, and must act through chess pieces. And you... are the most satisfactory chess piece it has found in a hundred thousand years... and also the most dangerous." Mo Xiansheng's voice carried an ineffable meaning, "Because you have emotion. You would spare nothing for Chen Nian. And this word 'emotion' is the only thing it cannot calculate."

Deep within the Tianji Record, that torn void had not fully healed. A wisp of consciousness transcending the Heavenly Dao lingered, flickering faintly between the pages. And in the instant Chen Ji turned to leave, that lingering consciousness suddenly fluctuated—as if whispering, as if anticipating. What Chen Ji didn't know was that at the moment he thought this dialogue had ended, the true 'gaze' of that Heavenly Eye had just begun. It was waiting. Waiting for him to find Chen Nian. Waiting for him to open the 'Tianji Box.' Waiting for the ending it had awaited for a hundred thousand years—whatever that ending might be.
